'''Robert M. Walker''' (February 6, 1929 – February 12, 2004) was an American [[physicist]],  a [[planetary scientist]], the founder and director of McDonnell Center for the Space Sciences at [[Washington University in St. Louis]], noted for his co-discovery of the etchability of nuclear particle tracks in solids,<ref name="Fleischer1975">R. L. Fleischer, P. Buford Price, and Robert M. Walker (1975) ''Nuclear Tracks in Solids'' (U. California Press, Berkeley).</ref> as well as his conjecture that [[meteorites]] and lunar rocks contain a record of the ancient radiation history of various stars including the [[Sun]].<ref name="NYT1">[https://www.nytimes.com/1990/09/04/science/big-science-it-worth-price-small-scale-science-feels-pinch-big-projects.html?scp=23&sq=&pagewanted=3 New York Times:Big Science; Is It Worth the Price?; Small-Scale Science Feels the Pinch From Big Projects; page 3 of 5;September 4, 1990]</ref><ref name="NYT2">[https://www.nytimes.com/1982/05/11/science/planes-soar-into-stratosphere-to-snare-bits-of-the-cosmic-past.html?scp=21&sq=&pagewanted=2 New York Times:PLANES SOAR INTO STRATOSPHERE TO SNARE BITS OF THE COSMIC PAST;page 2 of 3; May 11, 1982]</ref><ref name="NAS">[http://www.nap.edu/readingroom.php?book=biomems&page=rwalker.html National Academies Press:National Academy of Sciences;Biographical Memoirs;Robert M. Walker;By P. Buford Price and Ernst Zinner]</ref><ref name="WUSTL1">[http://presolar.wustl.edu/Laboratory_for_Space_Sciences/Robert_M_Walker.html Washington University in St. Louis;Robert M Walker;1929 - 2004]</ref><ref name="NYT3">[https://www.nytimes.com/1967/06/12/archives/union-college.html?sq=%2522Robert%2520M.%2520Walker%2522&scp=11&st=cse New York Times:Union College:Robert M, walker, director of the laboratory for space physics]</ref>
[[6372 Walker|Asteroid 6372]] was named Walker in his honor by the [[International Astronomical Union]].<ref name="NAS"/>
Walker was a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="NAS"/><ref name="WUSTL1"/>
Walker was also a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]],<ref name="WUSTL1"/> the [[American Geophysical Union]],<ref name="WUSTL1"/> the [[Meteoritical Society]]<ref name="WUSTL1"/> and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref name="WUSTL1"/> 
He was also a founder and the first president of Volunteers in Technical Assistance (VITA).<ref name="WUSTL1"/><ref name="NYT3"/>

== Notable distinctions ==
* 1964    [[American Nuclear Society]] Annual Award<ref name="WUSTL1"/> 
* 1966    [[Yale University|Yale]] Engineering Association Annual Award for Contributions to Basic and Applied Science<ref name="NAS"/><ref name="WUSTL1"/> 
* 1967    Doctor, honoris causa, [[Union College]]<ref name="NAS"/><ref name="NYT3"/>
* 1970    [[NASA]] Exceptional Scientific Achievement Award<ref name="NAS"/><ref name="WUSTL1"/> 
* 1971    E. O. Lawrence Memorial Award of the [[U.S. Atomic Energy Commission]]<ref name="NAS"/><ref name="WUSTL1"/> 
* 1973    Elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="NAS"/>
* 1975    Docteur, honoris causa, [[University of Clermont-Ferrand]], France<ref name="NAS"/>
* 1985    Antarctic Service Medal of the [[National Science Foundation]]<ref name="WUSTL1"/>
* 1991    J. Lawrence Smith Medal, [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="NAS"/><ref name="WUSTL1"/>
* 1992    Officier de l’Ordre des Palmes Academiques<ref name="NAS"/><ref name="WUSTL1"/>
* 1993    Leonard Medal of the [[Meteoritical Society]]<ref name="NAS"/><ref name="WUSTL1"/>
* 1997    Peter Raven Lifetime Achievement Award, St. Louis Academy of Science<ref name="NAS"/>
* 1999    [[6372 Walker|Asteroid 6372]] named Walker by [[International Astronomical Union]]<ref name="NAS"/><ref>{{cite book|chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/referenceworkentry/10.1007%2F978-3-540-29925-7_5826 |publisher=Springer |date=2003 |isbn=978-3-540-29925-7 |doi=10.1007/978-3-540-29925-7_5826 |chapter=(6372) Walker |title=Dictionary of Minor Planet Names |pages=528 }}</ref>
* 2004    Doctor, honoris causa (posthumous), [[Washington University in St. Louis]]<ref name="NAS"/>

== Life and career ==
* February 6, 1929, born in [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]]
* 1950 graduated from Union College with a degree in physics
* 1954 Ph.D. in physics, [[Yale University]]
* 1966 the McDonnell Professor of Physics, [[Washington University in St. Louis]]
* February 12, 2004 died in [[Brussels, Belgium]] [[stomach cancer]]

== Personal life ==
Walker was married to the cosmochemist [[Ghislaine Crozaz]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Sciences|first=National Academy of|url=https://www.nap.edu/catalog/11429/biographical-memoirs-volume-86|title=Biographical Memoirs: Volume 86|date=2005|isbn=978-0-309-10369-5|language=en|doi=10.17226/11429}}</ref>
